$comment: The committed registry of ALWAYS-ON agent routines (role-lens review, ai-ops next-work). Every recurring scheduled lane is declared here with its cadence, the human who authorized it, what it may write, where it stops and escalates, and where its firing evidence lands. scripts/check-scheduled-routines.mjs holds this file against the heartbeat artifacts and the org roster; its header states honestly that it gates the DECLARATION and the EVIDENCE OF FIRING — it cannot read the live account scheduler. Transcribed FROM the live scheduler (list_triggers) on 2026-08-21, not from memory. One-shot self-reminders (send_later check-ins) are deliberately out of scope: they are ephemeral work-pacing, not standing lanes.

Raise/clear/take ops ride the cycle's one lane:deliver batch.

routines.trigger: launchd:com.signalgrid.build-tick (installed by scripts/mac/install-build-tick.sh on the owner's Mac; not an account trigger)
routines.binding: launchd user agent on the Mac lane's machine, running scripts/mac/build-tick.sh (which pins SignalGrid_Alpha's sha once per run with git ls-remote of the real remote and re-execs that sha's copy); by default the script runs a STAGED pipeline of headless `claude -p` sessions (scripts/mac/build-tick-stages.mjs holds the one stage table; tiers follow DR-047 and the DR-060 stage table): triage on sonnet, READ-ONLY by tool absence (--tools Read,Grep,Glob; no Bash, Edit or Write); build on haiku, sonnet or opus by the kind triage names (mechanical, code, judgment; an unknown kind resolves to opus); review on opus, READ-ONLY by tool absence; at most one fix on the build's own tier, then a second review. Each stage uses --output-format json and caps per the helper's table (wall clock, turns, and a budget cap and opus fallback model that are UNVERIFIED on subscription auth), never bypassPermissions, and no session has git or GitHub credentials in its environment. The script, not a session, does every outward act Optional SG_STAGE_RUNNER is an explicitly configured absolute host executable outside the clone and writable run directory; its file identity and SHA256 are pinned and rechecked before each stage. It receives protocol-version-1 JSON on stdin (stage, kind, tierAsked, limits, readOnly, brief, runDir, cwd, base, schema), never a shell command. The trusted host transport must enforce read-only triage/review, fresh independent reviews, credentials, time/turn limits and its declared cost policy, refuse unsupported limits, and report the actual provider/model with unknown costs left null. Default Claude arguments stay unchanged; local-model contextual advice does not grant writer or merge authority.
routines.authorizationEvidence: owner in a Mac Claude Code session, 2026-09-29 (prior recorded owner approval; DR-061 remains a proposal): asked 'Should the Mac start a build session by itself every few hours when the brain has a buildable task? This uses your Claude usage.' he chose 'Yes, build it (Recommended) — The brain builds its top task unattended and opens PRs.' After the auto-mode classifier refused the build as an unattended agent, he confirmed explicitly: 'Build it, I confirm — You explicitly approve an unattended Claude agent on this Mac with push + PR rights.' The PR-refresh step (below) pushes to other mac/* PR heads, which widens the write scope past this tick's own branches; the owner's covering instruction for that, verbatim (owner, in the Mac Claude Code session of 2026-10-01 (session_01XJMTVvCtYFZVkhK4K5nRdc), to the Mac lane): "Just get the merges done whatever it needs I'll approve." This row reads that instruction as covering exactly one thing: re-merging origin/SignalGrid_Alpha into the owner's own open mac/* PR branches (a fast-forward merge onto the head, never merging a PR itself), and nothing wider. Owner reaffirmed worker adaptation and operation on 2026-10-21: "Ok now look at the repo and adjust local model to adapt the workers and have them run and look at the entire project and get things in order and aligned" and "I want the whole system to do what it needs to do"; the preceding request asks to use Codex and Claude Code when usage and credits are available. This authorizes the worker transport under adopted DR-050 placement and DR-060 delegation; it does not adopt pending DR-061, change native-port doctrine, or widen decision-path merge authority.
routines.writeScope: AFTER the pause check (a paused tick refreshes nothing) and BEFORE it picks a row it runs, once it lands (it is PR #1353, not on mainline yet; until then the tick logs that mainline has no pr-refresh.mjs and skips the refresh), mainline's scripts/mac/pr-refresh.mjs --max 1 (extracted from the mainline sha this run pinned, never a branch copy), which may push ONE fast-forward merge of origin/SignalGrid_Alpha onto ONE open mac/* PR head (never a mac/tick-* one), only after preflight and breadth exit 0 on that head; it also posts PR comments and raises hands, and its preflight runs that PR's code WITH credentials; a refresh failure or a refresh past its REFRESH_SECONDS cap never stops the build (the cap kills the refresh's whole process group, not only its launcher). The model sessions (build, fix) have only the tools Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob and Bash (--tools; no Task, Workflow, web, cron or messaging tool exists in them), and edit only their own clone <repo>.build (a `git clone --reference` of the person's repo with its own .git, so refs, config, stash and hooks are not shared with the person's checkout; its config rewritten and its tree reset to the pinned mainline sha every run) and a run directory under ~/Library/Caches/signalgrid/build-tick/runs/; triage and review edit nothing. Mainline is pinned ONCE per run (git ls-remote of the real remote, never a ref a session could repoint): the clone reset, the diff the reviewer reads, the changed-path list, the forbidden-path check, the landing classifier and an is-ancestor check before the push all use that one sha, and a run that cannot ask the remote does nothing ("skipped: origin unreachable"). Every script-side git call after a session ran goes through hooks-off git (a session can plant hooks) and reads the real objects (GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 and a GIT_GRAFT_FILE that points at nothing, exported by the script, so a replace ref or an info/grafts a session planted cannot make diff, merge-base or status show a substitute), and the clone's config, info/exclude, info/attributes, replace refs and grafts are rewritten or deleted at run start, after each writing session and again before the push (a session can write them straight into the clone's .git, which the git deny list never sees); CI's frozen-lockfile install is the lockfile guard for tick PRs. The helper makes LOCAL commits in that clone and appends one cost-ledger line per stage to ~/Library/Caches/signalgrid/build-tick/ledger.jsonl (and the run directory's own copy); it never pushes. A mechanical (haiku) change, which is a writer rerun or a doc-only edit, may touch only docs/** (never a *-ratchet.json) and artifacts/sync/live-sync-manifest.json: the helper hands back any other diff and writes that change's commit message and PR body itself (DR-060: never Haiku). The SCRIPT pushes ONE branch per run, mac/build-row-<rowId>-<stamp> (first as an empty claim at the pinned mainline sha, then fast-forwarded to the session's commit only when preflight and breadth both exit 0 with their exact full verdict lines and a sentinel naming that sha, pushed BY SHA to the origin URL read before any session, from a clean tree whose HEAD is the commit the gates ran on), opens ONE PR through scripts/mac/gh-pr.mjs, and raises hands through lane-deliver batch (straight to SignalGrid_Alpha). Nothing in it merges or force-pushes, its push runs with git hooks off (the repo's local pre-push hook is deliberately not run, because a session can edit hooks; CI's frozen-lockfile install is the lockfile guard for tick PRs), and it never edits the person's working tree or refs or the lane tick's worktree (it only fetches the pinned sha's objects into the person's object store and prunes stale worktree registrations, and once, on first run after this change, removes the old <repo>.build worktree it replaces with a clone). Enforced by the environment, the deny list and the script, not an OS boundary: a session that deliberately wrote its own push route could still escape — a `pnpm exec`/`node` one-liner re-pointing git at ssh and the on-disk keys, or code this script's own preflight then runs with credentials (a documented residual risk; no OS sandbox is claimed). The script refuses to land a change touching an owner-reserved or forbidden path, pauses itself (~/Library/Caches/signalgrid/build-tick/paused) when a session is broken (see escalationBoundary), and raises one hand for a run hung past HUNG_SECONDS, which scripts/mac/build-tick.sh derives from the refresh, the stage table and the preflight and breadth budgets (a typed hour count here would only drift). When a host stage runner is configured, its provider-specific sandbox must preserve these same role and credential limits. Requested model tier and actual provider/model are recorded separately. A subscription invocation cap is not a dollar cap; a transport must report which policy it enforces and leave unavailable dollar-cost telemetry unknown.
routines.escalationBoundary: builds only objective-state.json tasks[] rows no remote branch or open PR names; an unreadable task list, branch list or PR list stops the run rather than building blind; a session that is itself broken PAUSES the tick, where broken (build-tick-stages.mjs sessionBroken) means its envelope names an API error (api_error_status set, terminal_reason api_error, or is_error without an error_max_* cap, which is what a logged-out CLI prints) or it died with no envelope on an exit other than 0 or the wall-clock cap, and a turn or time cap is a hand, not a pause; a broken triage pauses BEFORE any claim is pushed, so that row stays unclaimed, while a build, fix or review that breaks after the claim pauses the tick and leaves that row's claim branch for a person; the branch and PR lists are re-read right before the claim, and a row taken during triage is skipped; a triage that finds a row blocked on the owner, a lab, a tenant, hardware or Docker raises a hand (the objective loop parks AWAITING/BLOCKED rows only once #1216 lands) and keeps the claim; an unparseable triage is built on opus, and an unparseable or capped review is a reject (DR-047); a build or fix session that stops (hand.txt, read after each of them), changes nothing, leaves no commit message/PR files, touches anything a mechanical change may not (outside docs/** and the sync manifest), or whose change fails preflight or breadth raises a hand (DR-054) for the Mac lane and leaves its claim branch for a person; a helper that fails (cannot read or render a brief, a failed git command, any exception that is not a content hand) or writes no verdict PAUSES the tick instead of raising a hand that would claim a new row every run; a build or fix session that edited and then capped or broke is not committed (broken pauses, capped hands); 144 origin-unreachable runs in a row (12 hours at the five-minute cadence; git ls-remote or the sha fetch failing; such a run does nothing) raise a hand
routines.heartbeatPathReason: each run's outcome is a pushed mac/build-row-* branch with its PR, or a raised hand; the Mac being awake is already watched by mac-lane-tick's 5-minute heartbeat. ponytail: a loaded-but-never-firing job is not caught here — add a heartbeat if that happens once.

routines.awaitingReason: Machinery ready and owner-authorized (2026-09-09, re-affirmed 2026-09-13 'Activate it now'). A same-session activation on 2026-09-13 was REVERTED (trigger deleted): it created the trigger BEFORE this active row reached SignalGrid_Alpha (a fire could not heartbeat — check-scheduled-routines fatals on a heartbeat for an awaiting routine) and before the dispatch->gauntlet->PR path was proven end-to-end. Re-activation follows the design order: land this row active on Alpha, prove a Slice-2 dry run, THEN create_trigger (DR-032; Codex #705). Activation is NOT yet mechanically landable and is Slice-3 ENGINEERING, not a runbook (BRAIN_CYCLE_DESIGN.md Slice 3): authorizedOn (2026-09-09) doubles as the gate's active-no-heartbeat clock, so a bare flip to active is already past the 168h bound (needs a gate activatedOn baseline, a scripts/** change); and lane-deliver writes only the heartbeat artifact and runs check-scheduled-routines PRE-commit without staging this file, while the gate FATALs on awaiting-activation + a heartbeat, so the first fire cannot atomically land its heartbeat and flip status (needs a dedicated activation path, not lane-deliver). create_trigger must still come AFTER the row and a proven Slice-2 dry run (registry-first). Until that Slice-3 code exists the row stays awaiting-activation, authorizedOn is NEVER overwritten (the 2026-09-13 go is in authorizationEvidence), and no trigger is created. awaitingSince (2026-09-09) is the watchdog baseline and is NOT reset to dodge the 30-day bound: if the bound is reached before activation lands, ACTIVATE, RETIRE the row with evidence, or ESCALATE — never restart the clock (DR-032; Codex #705, #708).

Forward-build keeps a wave of worker sessions building the backlog and lands code PRs after an adversarial review (a Sonnet reviewer plus an Opus refuter, the tiers DR-047 assigns; the pairing is the routine prompt's own rule, which gives a MECHANICAL docs-only PR the Sonnet review plus the CI docs gates and merges a heartbeat PR on the gating check alone), which is the 'security and code check validation for bugs' this row described, at a higher cadence; whether that equals the DR-032 lens-panel audit over a blackboard is this lane's judgment call, recorded here. Retiring the row records those facts instead of carrying a label past the bound the gate holds. The owner's activation consent of 2026-09-13 stands in authorizationEvidence; awaitingReason and awaitingSince are kept as the record of the wait and are inert for a retired row (the gate reads them only while status is awaiting-activation). routines.writeScope: Its only repository write is its own heartbeat at `artifacts/agent-heartbeats/dependabot-queue-review.json` each cycle; it has NO merge authority and no other write scope — it REVIEWS and TRIAGES Dependabot's own PRs and ESCALATES every merge to the owner; it never auto-merges. Dependabot PRs change `package.json`/`pnpm-lock.yaml`, which `check-owner-gated-surfaces.mjs` treats as safety-machinery-adjacent, so the merge stays an owner decision regardless of green CI. It never edits `.github/dependabot.yml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` by hand outside a Dependabot PR, or any file `check-owner-gated-surfaces.mjs` classifies SAFETY_MACHINERY/OWNER_RESERVED. routines.escalationBoundary: Escalates to the owner only for a major-version Dependabot PR that needs code changes to pass, or a run stuck in `action_required` needing the owner's one-time workflow approval (docs/OWNER_ACTIONS.md); a quiet week with nothing new and no PR older than its tolerance sends no owner message. routines.awaitingReason: Declared in this pass to close the gap the 2026-09-12 self-evaluation found; the account trigger is deliberately not created here because creating a recurring fresh-session cadence requires an EXPLICIT owner go (no consent is inferred from a build/evaluation directive), per the awaiting-activation contract this registry already uses for brain-cycle. routines.cronNote: Dependabot's own schedule is `.github/dependabot.yml`'s `interval: monthly` — this registry's `cronIntervalHours` (scripts/check-scheduled-routines.mjs) can only read every-N-minutes, hourly, every-N-hours, daily, or weekly-single-weekday shapes; it has no monthly primitive, and an unparseable cron on a non-retired routine fails this gate's own self-test floor. So the cron above is WEEKLY (Monday 09:00 UTC), not monthly: it checks the monthly-generated queue often enough that an open PR is never unreviewed for the 11 days the self-evaluation found, which is a tighter bound than monthly would give and the one the finding actually calls for.
